items.name: Bremelanotide
items.benefits: Demonstrated human benefit for the approved subcutaneous bremelanotide product: increased sexual desire and reduced distress associated with acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder in premenopausal women meeting the labeled criteria. This evidence does not establish benefits in men or postmenopausal women, or general sexual-performance enhancement.

source_statements.section: Who PT-141 Is For and Who Should Avoid It
source_statements.excerpt: The Vyleesi label and the Mayo Clinic drug summary state that PT-141 should not be used in people with uncontrolled hypertension or known cardiovascular disease, because of the transient blood pressure rise after dosing. It is also not recommended during pregnancy or while planning pregnancy, and there is no adequate safety data for breastfeeding.

source_statements.section: Who PT-141 Is For and Who Should Avoid It
source_statements.excerpt: Severe kidney or liver disease may slow clearance. Conditions that delay gastric emptying may worsen with PT-141 because melanocortin agonism slows gastric emptying. Naltrexone is listed as a notable interaction (PT-141 may reduce naltrexone exposure when both are used). PT-141 should not be combined with another melanocortin agonist such as Melanotan II, because the receptors overlap and the safety of combined exposure has not been

Side effect rates below come from the FDA-approved Vyleesi label and from the Phase 3 RECONNECT trial publication (Kingsberg 2019). The most common adverse event was nausea, reported by about 40% of bremelanotide users at the 1.75 mg dose. Most events were mild to moderate, decreased over time with repeat use, and did not lead to discontinuation in most participants.
